Automating property enquiries: website, advertising and CRM

How an enquiry becomes a deal with an owner and a next action. Integrations, notifications, processing rules and marketing feedback from RESET projects.

Automating property enquiries starts with a clear route: source, CRM, owner, task and contact outcome. The system should deliver a lead to the team and help turn it into an action. In one workflow we implemented for Delmar, an agent takes ownership and the CRM assigns responsibility, creates a task and sends a Telegram notification. Management sees who is handling the client; one action starts the process for the agent. Here we explain the connections, team rules and evaluation.

01

Why enquiries get lost between marketing and sales

Enquiries arrive through websites, ad forms, messengers, calls, property portals and referrals. Each has its own interface: information stays on staff phones, enters spreadsheets or waits to be exported. Manual collection makes it easy to miss a message or assume a colleague is handling it. Even a received enquiry can sit for days without a next action. We therefore examine the whole journey, including ownership and follow-up.

These gaps also affect marketing and sales. Marketers see lead counts, agents remember unsuccessful calls, and managers wonder why spending has not produced the expected deals. Without a processing history, discussion becomes competing impressions. A shared system shows arrival time, ownership and subsequent events, giving the team evidence to discuss actions and lead quality.

02

Connecting people, marketing and infrastructure

RESET considers three elements: team, marketing and tools. The team defines roles and procedures, marketing attracts enquiries and analyses outcomes, and infrastructure transfers data and triggers agreed actions. An ad integration cannot fix missing assignment rules. Rules alone do not remove manual work if information stays scattered. We describe the process before choosing integrations.

We build these connections in property projects including Shepit House and continue developing them for Delmar. Each team has its own channels and requirements. Here we describe Delmar's link between enquiry receipt, ownership and an automatic task. Internal distribution rules are outside this article: they are agreed with the client and cannot sensibly be copied to another agency without reviewing its process.

03

Getting website and advertising enquiries into a CRM

The first step is automatic transfer without copying. Website forms need agreed fields, source tracking and post-submission behaviour. Ad lead forms need a supported connection to the chosen system. For Meta we use its supported lead mechanisms; a webhook example appears in the official Meta sample repository. The aim is prompt automatic delivery; actual timing depends on the services and integration.

Calls, portals and referrals need individual consideration. One channel may have a connector, another need telephony, and an employee may enter a referral manually. Agree how each joins the shared records with a source. Test an enquiry all the way to its record, task and notification. Check repeat enquiries so an existing client does not become several disconnected records.

04

Automatic task assignment at Delmar

In this workflow, an enquiry appears in the CRM and staff receive a notification. An agent opens it and takes ownership. Each enquiry needs one owner so responsibility is clear. Assignment automatically creates a calendar task and sends the agent a Telegram notification. Management can see the task and responsible employee.

This removes repetitive work: the agent need not create a separate task, choose a date and copy the client's details into a reminder. Agreed rules provide the next step alongside responsibility. When it is time to contact the client, a reminder brings the task back to attention. Afterwards, the agent records the result so the history remains clear to both agent and manager.

A new lead’s route in the Delmar workflow
EventSystem actionTeam outcome
Enquiry receivedAdds it to the CRM and notifies staffThe team sees the new lead
Agent claims the enquiryAssigns one ownerClear responsibility
Owner assignedCreates a calendar task and sends a Telegram alertThe next step is prepared
Action becomes dueReminds the ownerThe agent returns to the client
Agent records the outcomeUpdates the enquiry historyManagement and marketing see progress

This runs in our Estate CRM, shown in the Delmar case study. Similar workflows in an off-the-shelf CRM depend on features, plans and integrations. Describe the events and actions first, then check the product to distinguish built-in functionality from required development. See our article on choosing a property agency CRM.

05

What should happen after a lead arrives?

For inbound advertising enquiries, RESET recommends aiming for first contact within five minutes. This is our working target, to be agreed with staffing and opening hours. Overnight enquiries need a separate response procedure. Define when timing starts and what counts as contact. Otherwise, reports may show rapid assignment while the client is still waiting for a call.

After the first attempt, establish a follow-up protocol. Agree attempt counts, intervals and channels; for example, three attempts at different times. Respect the client's preferences, available details and response. An incorrect number is a distinct reason to record. If the person asks to speak later, save the agreement and schedule a reminder.

06

What if nobody takes the enquiry or the agent does not act?

Rules are also needed for interrupted workflows. Define how long an enquiry can remain unassigned, who sees it and who is alerted. Distinguish a client's silence from an employee's inaction. The former needs the next protocol step; the latter may require an overdue-work alert. Escalation, reassignment and duty arrangements are agreed separately.

Automatic reassignment only suits predefined conditions. Unexpectedly switching an agent who is already speaking with a client can disrupt agreements and create duplicate calls. Keep assignment history, contact outcomes and transfer reasons. A small team may only need a manager notification and manual decision. More complex rules must remain understandable to everyone involved.

07

Which CRM data marketing needs

To judge advertising quality, marketers need to know how enquiries were handled. If the first call came two days later and the next a week later, rejection cannot easily be attributed solely to advertising. Arrival time, contact time, attempts, conversation results and deal stages matter. With the agreed protocol followed, this history helps marketing and sales evaluate the audience and offer and adjust campaigns.

What to track alongside lead volume and cost
MetricQuestion answered
Arrival and first contact timesHow quickly did the team respond?
Owner and next taskWho is responsible and what is planned?
Contact attempts and outcomesWas the agreed procedure followed?
Qualification and deal stageDoes the request fit and how is it progressing?
Reason for rejection or postponementWhy did progress stop and is follow-up needed?
Source and campaignWhich channels bring suitable clients?

Separate uncontacted enquiries, unsuitable requests, postponed decisions and clients reaching selection or viewing. Their reasons and next actions differ. “Poor-quality lead” without explanation offers little guidance. Shared qualification criteria enable consistent reporting and channel comparisons. See Facebook and Instagram leads for the connection with advertising.

08

Returning to buyers who postponed a decision

Some buyers delay because of timing, budget or personal circumstances. Closing their deal without explanation loses context. We recommend a follow-up stage with the reason and next contact date. The agent then understands what changed and what offer is appropriate. A suitable property may prompt one conversation; a previously agreed date may prompt another.

Automation saves the task and reminds the agent. The message still needs to reflect the person's request and previous agreements. Before sending a property, check the previously discussed budget and area. Record the new outcome so the next step uses current information. Measure reactivation using the agency's own data, distinguishing renewed contact from a completed deal.

09

Implementation and checks

We map channels and enquiry routes, then agree notifications, assignment, task creation and management visibility. After connecting services, we send test enquiries through the full sequence: fields, sources, assignment, calendar and notifications. For a custom system, also check two employees attempting to claim the same enquiry simultaneously.

Test errors too: repeat submissions, unavailable services and delayed notifications. Staff need to know where to check if a message does not arrive. The CRM remains the record even when messenger delivery fails. After launch, review real enquiries and staff understanding, refine rules and remove distracting notifications.

10

What enquiry automation costs

When RESET launches advertising or implements a CRM, agreed automation is included in that scope. For Meta, we define enquiry delivery; for a CRM, tasks and notifications. The client sees the complete implementation and which actions are automatic. Additional scenarios are quoted separately. External licences, telephony and recurring fees depend on the solution.

How RESET prices automation
SituationCost and terms
Meta advertising launchAgreed automation is included in the advertising scope
CRM implementation or developmentAgreed workflows are included in the CRM estimate
Connecting an existing third-party systemAround $200-500 for agreed scope after diagnosis
New modules or complex logicQuoted individually
Paid external servicesLicences, telephony and subscriptions are separate

For an existing system built by another team, we start with diagnosis. Individual connections may cost around $200-500, depending on access, service capabilities and logic. Sometimes a form-to-CRM connection is enough; sometimes data structures or procedures need repair first. Timing follows that assessment and the agreed scope. The client should know the triggers, maintenance responsibility and included work.

11

Where an agency should begin

Follow one ordinary enquiry from its source to the next client contact. Find manual copying, the moment ownership appears and who notices delays. Describe the desired sequence and actions governed by clear rules. This produces a concrete automation brief and shows whether the current CRM is enough. RESET connects those actions with marketing and team workflows so each recorded enquiry has an owner, a next step and a clear history.
